title: Chem lab checklist — live founder regression
raw_input: I was the fastest student in our AP chem lab section at finishing titration setups. During one lab, a classmate copied my setup and contaminated her sample because I had skipped labeling one transfer step I always did in my head. My teacher said speed was not the same thing as reliability. The next week I built a one-page checklist and made everyone use it before touching the burette. Our failed trials dropped a lot, and I stopped being proud of finishing first.
expected_founder_acceptance: Page 3 title is decisive and not stitched from raw fragments.
Page 3 explanation is evidence-led and not truncated.
Page 4 is evidence-first and does not leak internal framework language.
expected_failure_mode_to_watch: Malformed stitched title or packet/render mismatch on Page 3.

title: Robotics pit decision under pressure
raw_input: During regionals our robot failed inspection twice, and I told the team to remove an autonomous feature to pass on time. Another programmer argued we should keep it and risk a late match. I overruled him. We qualified but lost our quarterfinal because of manual control mistakes. After the event he said my call protected schedule but ignored our actual strength. I now frame emergency decisions as tradeoffs out loud before choosing.
expected_founder_acceptance: Recommendation names the real tradeoff and decision standard clearly.
Why-this-wins is case-specific and draftable.
Opening guidance stays evidence-first.
expected_failure_mode_to_watch: Generic stronger/weaker comparison or flattened decision language.

title: Benefits office translation responsibility
raw_input: I used to think translating for my grandparents at government offices was just a family duty. At one appointment the clerk spoke quickly and I summarized instead of translating line by line so we could finish faster. My grandfather signed a form he did not understand. We had to return the next week to reverse it. Since then I ask officials to pause and I translate every instruction fully even when the line gets longer. That day changed what responsibility sounds like to me.
expected_founder_acceptance: Page 3 chooses one believable center instead of generic growth language.
Evidence anchoring reflects the misunderstanding and correction.
Page 4 guidance starts from the proof-bearing scene.
expected_failure_mode_to_watch: Surface drift back to generic responsibility narration.

title: Robotics reliability vs restaurant leadership
raw_input: I keep circling between two things. One is robotics where I stopped chasing speed and started building checklists after our test runs kept failing. The other is helping at my family's restaurant where I started training younger cousins because I realized me doing everything fast was creating more confusion. Both feel true and I do not know which one is stronger for my essay yet.
expected_founder_acceptance: The output does not split the difference lazily.
The recommendation feels like a real judgment call.
The rendered recommendation stays case-specific across compare logic.
expected_failure_mode_to_watch: Fallback or ranking drift produces stitched or generic compare output.
